sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Brij Bhushan Upadhyay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ramesh Kumar Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 593 of 2015 at Police Station-Colonelganj, District-Prayagraj under Sections 419, 420, 406, 376 IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 22.06.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 07.08.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Brij Bhushan Upadhyay, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Ramesh Kumar, learned counsel on behalf of the informant and Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Narottam Prasad vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189491391/

sentences.text: 1. Delay in lodgement of the F.I.R. in the facts and circumstances of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
2. The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy and consensual physical relations with the applicant.
3. The F.I.R. was lodged at the behest of her husband after their relationship got exposed.
The criminal case is being leveraged to extract money from applicant.
4. The victim has also filed a petition before this Court for quashment of the FIR.
5. After investigations, the applicant was exonerated.
A final report was filed by the police before the trial court.
6. The victim had other love interest and a child was born from that union.
7. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
8. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
9. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of her influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Narottam Prasad be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Jaswant  Narottam Prasad vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189491391/
